record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: How can one determine, in a robust and practically usable way, when a finite-density QCD method that is formally correct in principle is actually failing in practice and producing unphysical answers? This includes identifying diagnostics that distinguish trustworthy results from artifacts caused by pitfalls such as hidden overlap problems, uncontrolled phase fluctuations, or other failures of methods that are mathematically sound but numerically unreliable.

evidence.quote: The difficulty in the study of theories with the sign problem is that the numerical methods which are correct in principle do not necessarily work in practice and it is hard to know when it fails.

Another possible reason is that, when the cures to the sign problem are discussed, formally correct arguments can lead to practically wrong results, and it is hard to figure out when such things happen.

artifact.status_search_result: No general solution is known. Reviews on the lattice QCD sign problem (2021–2025) consistently describe the diagnosis of silent failures in formally-correct methods (overlap problem, complex-Langevin boundary terms, missed thimbles) as an active and unresolved research area, with only partial, method-specific criteria available (e.g., Aarts–Seiler–Stamatescu boundary-term and drift-distribution criteria for complex Langevin). A unified, robust diagnostic framework remains open.

status_evidence.title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical methods which are correct in principle do not necessarily work in practice and it is hard to know when it fails.
status_evidence.claim: The diagnosis of silent failure of formally-correct methods is identified as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Complex Langevin and boundary terms (Aarts, Seiler, Stamatescu and follow-ups)
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary-term and drift-distribution criteria provide partial, method-specific diagnostics for complex Langevin correctness.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial, method-specific diagnostic criteria currently exist.
